cancel_path_architecture.evidence: (a) No busy leak: SlotLease::drop always ends in release_inner (src/resident_worker_pool.rs:685), which clears slot.busy (src/resident_worker_pool.rs:652-654); the RAII drop covers every drop point of the pinned future in backend.rs:275. (b) No double decrement: active_leases.fetch_sub (src/resident_worker_pool.rs:651) is inside release_inner, guarded by the released-AtomicBool CAS at :644-650, so the explicit release() in the entry points (src/resident_worker_pool.rs:317/:345) and the Drop are mutually exclusive. (c) No cross-lease retirement: the per-slot busy CAS in acquire_lease (src/resident_worker_pool.rs:372-378) is the exclusive lease, so no concurrent dispatch can hold or re-lease the slot while our lease lives; the retirement record in Drop (src/resident_worker_pool.rs:670-684) precedes the busy clear at :685, and a waiter can only observe the free slot after the record is written. The settled flag (src/resident_worker_pool.rs:492, :670) keeps a last-instant race where dispatch finished and settle already ran from double-recording. (d) Temp-dir reclaim: per-request RequestTemp is an owned tempfile::TempDir created before dispatch (src/resident_worker.rs:266); on cancellation the worker future is dropped mid-run, so TempDir's RAII drop removes the directory (settle/close is the explicit variant at src/resident_worker.rs:740-751); the worker process tree is reaped by KillOnDrop (src/resident_worker.rs:5, :159). summary: The merge bcea113 landed the owner-adjudicated semantics exactly: the manager is now a thin pool facade with the ef7e6ef manager-level cancellation machinery removed, backend.rs owns cancellation via a select! that drops the pool.dispatch future and relies on the pool's RAII SlotLease to retire the slot, reap the worker, and release the lease synchronously, with the CLI-shaped exit_code -1 response.
